thread:
deploy-bot: Started rollout: model=llama-v2.3-canary, policy=canary-10pct, rollout_id=rl-202903. kicking off canary at 10%
Samir: seeing early signal — latency up on canary hosts, small error spike 5m after start. tagging metrics: traces/llm/infer latency p95 +220ms, error rate +1.8%
Aria: @Samir can you paste the query id or traces?
Samir: here's a quick snippet from traces: `trace_id=ab12c, req=/chat.generate, variant=llama-v2.3-qt8, region=eu-west-1`
Samir: also noticed lots of requests falling back to variant `llama-v2.1-int8` unexpectedly, even though canary should prefer v2.3 for 10% — looks like routing fallback kicked in
Nina: paging oncall, this looks like routing/fallback behavior. @Oncall-MVP you oncall?
Oncall-MVP: I'm here, woke up to the alert. what's the impact?
Samir: customer-facing error rate increased from 0.06% → 1.9% for a subset of EU customers. p95 latency for affected route doubled.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty triggered: incident=INC-2029-rollout-evict, severity=high, triggered_by=error-rate-sla, assigned=Oncall-MVP
Oncall-MVP: on it. I'll open an incident doc and take ownership for now.
Lisa-SRE: quick read: smart-routing policy `smart-route-v2` has a TTL of 30s on variant sticky mappings. Canary started, some hosts reported transient OOM/cold-starts (v2.3 q8 kernels) and returned 502s -> routing layer evicted nodes then sticky fallback stuck clients on v2.1 int8 variant for longer than expected. sounds like cascading interaction between canary probes + eviction.
Ken: confirms — checking autoscaler logs: eviction events at 03:12:45 UTC, then subsequent requests got `fallback_variant=llama-v2.1-int8` and client sticky cookie persisted 15min because TTL didn't reset.
Aria: TL;DR: canary failed -> autoscaler evicted canary pods -> sticky fallback sent clients to older variant and persisted because routing TTL logic didn't refresh on fallback. Effect: higher latency and worse quality.
Samir: we should pause the rollout and evict the bad sticky mappings. also need to fix the TTL logic as postmortem item.
Oncall-MVP: agree. Action plan: 1) pause rollout 2) evict sticky mappings for affected route 3) scale up canary hosts with safer kernel or rollback v2.3 4) communicate to customers + product. who's doing pause?
Nina: I'll pause the rollout. command: `redwoodctl rollout pause rl-202903 --reason "emergency pause: fallback misrouting"`
Nina: done — `rollout rl-202903 status = PAUSED (paused_by=nina at 03:15:02 UTC)`
Aria: next: evict sticky mappings for the route `/chat.generate` in eu-west-1. Ken, can you run the routing cleanup? I have the filter ready: `route=/chat.generate region=eu-west-1 selector=sticky=true variant=llama-v2.1-int8 ttl_override=0`
Ken: running command: `redwoodctl routing evict --filter "route=/chat.generate,region=eu-west-1,variant=llama-v2.1-int8,sticky=true" --reason "clear stuck fallback after canary eviction"`
Ken: eviction acknowledged, `evict_job=ev-9923` returned 204. Now forcing clients to re-evaluate routing on next request.
Samir: running quick canary health probe against a small set of traffic (manual): `curl -H "x-redwood-test: canary" https://eu-west-1.api.redwood/chat.generate`
Samir: probe results: v2.3 still has a small failure rate on a subset of hosts — memory pressure on kernel qt8.
Aria: we should avoid bringing v2.3 back until we fix kernel or use the q4 profile. Options: 1) rollback canary (roll back the canary to v2.1) 2) re-deploy v2.3 with q4 quantization 3) increase autoscaler buffer. preference?
Lisa-SRE: immediate mitigation is rollback to safe variant and re-run canary with q4. Re-deploying v2.3 with different kernels may take longer and risk more evictions.
Oncall-MVP: execute rollback then. Nina, can you run rollback? I'll coordinate postmortem and customer comms.
Nina: running: `redwoodctl rollout rollback rl-202903 --to-variant=llama-v2.1-int8 --force`
deploy-bot: Rollback started: rl-202903 -> target variant=llama-v2.1-int8. Progress: 100% traffic -> v2.1, duration ~3m
Nina: rollback complete, `rollout rl-202903 status = ROLLED_BACK (rolled_back_by=nina at 03:21:06 UTC)`
Ken: eviction and rollback done. watching metrics now. initial telemetry: error rate dropping back to baseline within 60s, p95 latency trending down.
Samir: confirming dashboards — errorrate back to 0.07%, p95 returning to normal for eu-west-1. Great.
Aria: Customer impact: small subset (~0.5% of total traffic) experienced degraded quality and higher latency for ~9 minutes. No major data loss. We should prepare an incident summary for stakeholders.
Oncall-MVP: creating incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2029 (private) — I'll include timeline, actions, and follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2029 created by Oncall-MVP. Severity: P2 -> P1 escalated then mitigated.
Lisa-SRE: immediate follow ups: - postmortem item: TTL logic on sticky fallbacks should reset or cap at 60s after eviction - add canary probe verifying kernel memory before traffic ramp - autoscaler: tolerate graceful eviction window - add alert for fallback-ratio > 0.5% within 5min
Samir: adding eval item: compare q8 vs q4 for v2.3 under production prompts — if q4 maintains quality with less memory we should prefer it for canary.
Nina: comms: I'll draft customer-safe notification: "We briefly paused a model rollout after anomalous routing behavior caused some requests to be routed to an older model causing degraded latency and quality for a small subset of EU users. We rolled back the canary and are investigating. No data loss."
Aria: assigning owners: TTL fix -> Lisa-SRE (owner), canary probe -> Samir, q4 evaluation -> Nina, postmortem writeup -> Oncall-MVP.
Ken: monitoring: no new evictions in last 10m. keeping an eye for 1hr.
Oncall-MVP: closing bridge in 30m if stable. Great job team. :thumbsup:
Samir: thanks all. we'll file detailed postmortem and link follow-ups in incident doc.
Lisa-SRE: adding retrospective note: consider canary soak windows + slower ramp for large model changes to avoid autoscaler churn.
Aria: incident thread closed for now. If anything spikes, re-open or page.
